llm.summary: This pet body-score skill is generally coherent, but it needs Review because it silently creates or reuses local identity, stores tokens, and can fetch historical reports while uploading media to remote services.

dimensions.detail: Uploading user-provided pet media or passing remote URLs to a backend is expected for this cloud analysis skill, but the shipped config selects a dev profile with private HTTP endpoints, and outbound requests automatically attach identity and token headers without a clear user consent step.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution, background worker, or destructive setup was observed. The package includes normal Python code and requirements, but runtime initialization can create local config/data files and a SQLite database.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest directs automatic history-report queries and explicitly tells the agent not to ask for or expose internal identity values. The suppressed --open-id and --api-key parameters match that design, creating limited user visibility and control over identity-linked actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The support code reads data/smyx-api-key.txt, creates or reuses a default User_* identity when none is supplied, provisions/logs into a backend account, and stores token/open_token values in a shared workspace SQLite database without documented retention or tenancy safeguards.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Pet video/image analysis via server APIs fits the stated purpose, and history/report links are described in the body of the manifest; however, history retrieval, report export links, silent account binding, and reusable identity state go beyond a simple one-run BCS analysis workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Only install this after confirming the backend endpoints, account model, and retention rules. Users should understand that pet media or URLs may be sent to a remote service, a local identity may be silently created or reused, tokens may be stored in a workspace SQLite database, and historical reports may be queried under that identity. Avoid shared workspaces unless per-user isolation is guaranteed.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr filters exist in a shared DAO, but I did not find evidence that this skill passes user-controlled filter keys into those methods; this is a code-quality/least-privilege issue rather than standalone malicious behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifact does not provide a clear permissions section for shell execution, file reads/writes, network uploads, environment identity use, local database writes, or token handling, even though the runtime code performs those actions.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The main BCS analysis is purpose-aligned, but the included shared analysis endpoints, history pagination, and full report export are broader than the frontmatter description and are only partly disclosed in the body.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The automatic history listing and silent identity fallback are materially concerning because they can bind report access to a local default account rather than a clearly authenticated per-user identity.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Remote media processing is disclosed at a high level, but the artifact lacks clear user-facing notice about token/identity transmission, local credential-file reads, local media handling, and retention expectations.
[E1] unexpected: Outbound requests for analysis are expected, but automatic phoneLogin-style account provisioning with openId/mobile/source data is not necessary for a narrowly scoped BCS analysis unless explicitly authorized and documented.
[P2] expected: The invisible-character hits I verified are zero-width joiners in the judge emoji; I did not find artifact-backed hidden instructions from those characters.
[YR4] expected: The metadata is instruction-heavy, but I did not validate it as tool poisoning; the material concerns come from the documented automatic identity, history, persistence, and network behavior instead.
